question: During fetal cardiac screening, a murmur prompts evaluation. The baby is found to have a defect in neural crest migration affecting conotruncal septation. Which defect is expected?
explanation: The membranous part of the interventricular septum is formed largely by the conotruncal (aorticopulmonary) septum, which is derived from neural crest cells. When neural crest migration is defective, the conotruncal septum does not fuse properly with the muscular interventricular septum -> membranous ventricular septal defect (VSD). Neural crest defects classically cause: Membranous VSD, Tetralogy of Fallot, Persistent truncus arteriosus, Transposition of great arteries. ASD and mitral atresia do not involve neural crest. Aortic stenosis is valvular and not due to conotruncal migration failure.

question: Which of the following is the primary anatomical abnormality in transposition of the great arteries?

options.A: Aortic arch lies anterior to the pulmonary trunk
options.B: Aorta arises from the right ventricle
options.C: Pulmonary trunk arises from the right ventricle
options.D: Aortic arch lies posterior to the pulmonary trunk
